text:
laura_cs: Hey team — customer on Dedicated reporting massive 5-10s tail latency spikes and 429s during morning traffic ramp. They say autoscale didn't add nodes quickly, requests queued. Raising for investigation.

mike_oncall: Thanks @laura_cs — can you paste repro steps + any logs from the customer's tenant? Is this a one-off or repeated every day?

laura_cs: Repro steps from customer: run 200 concurrent generation requests to dedicated endpoint for their workspace. Example:
```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST https://dedicated.api.redwood/customer-123/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt":"short"}' &
done
wait
```
They attached agent logs showing many requests stuck on queues and repeated 502/503s from warmup hook.

sam_runtime: I pulled the platform autoscaler logs for that tenant during the incident window (2026-02-14 08:03-08:12 UTC). Key snippets: 
```
autoscaler: desired_replicas=8 current_replicas=2 pending_provision=6
node-provisioner: started instance i-abc123 (initializing)
warmup-hook: call to /private/warmup returned 401 Unauthorized
kube: node i-abc123 NotReady (warmup-failed)
autoscaler: cannot count node i-abc123 towards ready replicas
autoscaler: scaling halted, reached max_concurrent_warmups=3
```
Looks like instances boot but warmup hook fails auth and nodes never join Ready set; autoscaler stops because we limit concurrent warmups to avoid thundering herd.

tom_infra: Confirmed in infra events: image-pull was fine, but the warmup container hits a signed request to customer's S3/KMS and the KMS call is failing with "AccessDenied" for the instance profile. That'll make the app fail healthchecks.

anna_eng: Two things to note: 1) the autoscaler has a safety cap of max_concurrent_warmups to reduce cost/spot churn; if many nodes are stuck by warmup errors, overall ready capacity doesn't grow. 2) customer min_replicas=2 and max_replicas=10, target_util=75%. Because warmup fails, controller never counts new nodes so the controller thinks it's still 2/10 but also stops launching new ones until some warmups free up. Edge case.

laura_cs: The customer also mentioned auth errors started after they rotated an internal KMS key yesterday. Could be permission mismatch.

mike_oncall: Short-term mitigation for customer: 1) manual scale to N=6 via console (bypass autoscaler) or set max_concurrent_warmups to 10 for their tenant. 2) Or route ramping traffic to hosted fallback so dedicated doesn't get overloaded. Which do they prefer?

laura_cs: Customer asked for automated fix — they want us to patch service so warmup failures don't block scaling. Also wants step-by-step repro for their security team.

sam_runtime: Suggested permanent fixes: - make warmup auth calls resilient (retry + backoff) and mark node Ready if core runtime responds even if optional warmup fails, or make warmup async post-ready. - add an admin override to ignore warmup hook for specific tenants. - increase observability: per-warmup failure reasons surfaced in console.

tom_infra: Immediate action I'm taking: adding a temporary tenant-level override to max_concurrent_warmups, and spinning up 4 manual instances for customer so they clear queue. Will also open infra PR to log KMS errors with instance-id.

autoscale-bot: [event] manual_scale:tenant=customer-123 from=2 to=6 by=tom_infra at=1823456900

anna_eng: After manual scale we should watch for regressions. Also propose we add a sanity check in autoscaler: if warmup-hook consistently fails with 401/403, treat as auth config issue and notify customer + pause warmup gating so we can still scale.

laura_cs: I'll inform the customer about manual scale + follow-ups. Adding them to a short postmortem and KMS rotation checklist. thx :) :thumbsup:
